title: ViewDefinition
description:
A declarative UI definition structure for building dynamic, data-driven layouts.

`ViewDefinition` provides a flexible, JSON-serializable way to define user interface layouts
that can be rendered dynamically at runtime. It's designed for building data-driven UIs,
server-driven rendering, or any scenario where UI structure needs to be defined outside of code.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this view definition.

Automatically generated UUID string.

title.description:
The title or name of this layout.

Used for documentation, debugging, or display in development tools.

type.description:
Determines how child views are arranged.

- SeeAlso: `LayoutType`

spacing.description: Spacing between root-level views in points.

padding.description:
Padding around the entire layout.

Can specify:
- Single value: `[20]` - all sides
- Two values: `[16, 20]` - vertical, horizontal
- Three values: `[16, 20, 24]` - top, horizontal, bottom
- Four values: `[10, 15, 20, 15]` - top, right, bottom, left

bgColor.description: Background color for the entire layout.

bgImage.description: Background image path for the entire layout.

width.description: Fixed width for the layout in points.

height.description: Fixed height for the layout in points.

frame.description:
Frame constraints for the entire layout.

- SeeAlso: `Frame`

custom.description:
Custom properties for extension and specialized behavior.

Allows passing arbitrary configuration data.

views.description:
The main content views to render.

These views are rendered in the foreground according to the `type` layout.

bgViews.description:
Background views rendered behind the main content.

Useful for creating layered effects, background images, or decorative elements.

debug.description:
Enable debug mode for development and troubleshooting.

When `true`, may display:
- View boundaries
- Layout guides
- Data binding information
- Performance metrics

LayoutType.title: LayoutType
LayoutType.description:
The type of layout container for arranging child views.

Layout types determine how child views are arranged and displayed within
the view definition.

Alignment.title: Alignment
Alignment.description:
Content alignment options for views within their container.

Alignment determines how content is positioned within its allocated space.

ImageResizeMode.title: ImageResizeMode
ImageResizeMode.description:
How images should be scaled and fitted within their bounds.

Image resize modes control how image content fills or fits its container.

Frame.title: Frame
Frame.description:
Layout constraints and sizing information for a view.

`Frame` provides fine-grained control over view dimensions, constraints,
and layout behavior.

width.description:
Fixed width in points.

When set, the view will have exactly this width.

height.description:
Fixed height in points.

When set, the view will have exactly this height.

minWidth.description:
Minimum width constraint in points.

The view will never be smaller than this width.

maxWidth.description:
Maximum width constraint in points.

The view will never be larger than this width.

minHeight.description:
Minimum height constraint in points.

The view will never be smaller than this height.

maxHeight.description:
Maximum height constraint in points.

The view will never be larger than this height.

aspectFit.description:
Aspect ratio for fitting content (width / height).

When set, the view maintains this aspect ratio while fitting within constraints.

aspectFill.description:
Aspect ratio for filling content (width / height).

When set, the view maintains this aspect ratio while filling its container.

layoutPriority.description:
Layout priority for resolving conflicts.

Higher values mean the view is less flexible. Used when multiple
views compete for space.

View.title: View
View.description:
A single view component within a view definition.

`View` represents an individual UI element that can be rendered. Views can be
nested to create complex layouts, bound to data, styled, and configured with
conditional visibility.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this view.

Automatically generated UUID string. Used for tracking, animations,
and list identification.

title.description:
The title or label for this view.
Used as:
- Label text
- Tab titles
- Button text

value.description:
Static value or template string for this view.

The interpretation depends on `type`:
- For `.text`: The text to display
- For `.image`: The image path or URL

type.description:
Determines how this view is displayed and what properties are relevant.

- SeeAlso: `ViewType`

attribute.description:
Data binding path for dynamic content.

Specifies which property from the data context to display or bind to.
Uses dot notation to access nested properties.

## Example
``json
// Simple property
"attribute": "data.level"

// Nested property
"attribute: "data.character.abilities.strength"
``

attributeType.description:
SystemType or Entity for the attribute value.

Helps renderers format and validate data appropriately.

context.description:
The data context scope for attribute resolution.

- SeeAlso: `ContextType`

style.description:
Style identifier for this view.

References a theme style definition that controls typography, colors,
spacing, and other visual properties.

link.description:
Navigation link

When tapped, navigates to the specified destination.

alignment.description:
Content alignment within this view's bounds.

- SeeAlso: `Alignment`

spacing.description:
Spacing between child views in points.

Only relevant for stack layouts (vStack, hStack, etc.).

padding.description:
Padding around the view's content.

Can specify:
- Single value: `[20]` - all sides
- Two values: `[16, 20]` - vertical, horizontal
- Three values: `[16, 20, 24]` - top, horizontal, bottom
- Four values: `[10, 15, 20, 15]` - top, right, bottom, left

color.description:
Text or foreground color.

Supports hex colors

borderWidth.description: Draws a border of this thickness around the view.

borderEdges.description:
Which edges should display the border.

Array of edge identifiers: `"top"`, `"right"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`.

cornerRadius.description: Corner radius in points for rounded corners.

imageResizeMode.description:
How images should be scaled within this view.

Only relevant for image-based views.

- SeeAlso: `ImageResizeMode`

width.description:
Fixed width in points.

Overrides the default width calculation.

height.description:
Fixed height in points.

Overrides the default height calculation.

frame.description:
Frame constraints for this view.

Provides fine-grained control over sizing and layout behavior.

- SeeAlso: `Frame`

visibleIf.description:
Condition for visibility - view shown when this evaluates to true.

Expression string evaluated against the data context.

## Example
``json
"visibleIf": "data.hp > 0"
"visibleIf": "data.level >= 5"
"visibleIf": "data.equipment.count > 0"
``

hiddenIf.description:
Condition for hiding - view hidden when this evaluates to true.

Expression string evaluated against the data context.

## Example
``json
"hiddenIf": "data.isGM == false"
"hiddenIf": "data.inventory.length == 0"
``

custom.description:
Custom properties for extension and specialized rendering.

Allows passing arbitrary configuration data to custom renderers
or view types.

action.description:
Action configuration for interactive views.

Defines what happens when the view is interacted with (tapped, submitted, etc.).

views.description:
Child views nested within this view.

Forms a tree structure for complex layouts.

ViewType.title: ViewType
ViewType.description:
The type of UI component to render.

View types are categorized into layout containers, content elements,
interactive controls, and specialized components.

ContextType.title: ContextType
ContextType.description:
The data context scope for this view.

Context type determines where the view looks for data when evaluating
attribute bindings and visibility conditions.
